page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by two Intel Xeon 8259CL processors. It features 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. The server delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 82,018.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 58,133.28, placing it in the top tier of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 4,542.25 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 224.19 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations are highly performant, with PassMark database operations scoring 22,158.48 and Redis SET operations reaching 76.05 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is average, and without GPU acceleration, LLM text generation speeds are poor, scoring 5.12 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

Given its bare-metal architecture, high memory density, and fast local NVMe storage, this server offers high resource density for workloads requiring direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead. The combination of 100 Gbps network throughput and large local storage makes it highly suitable for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, high-throughput static web serving, and data-intensive enterprise applications.
